newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen rising.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed 0.18 up in the kerb market at 40.20 to the dollar on Wednesday on an inflow of dollars from abroad, dealers said.

They said the rupee was likely to open up on Thursday if the market was not closed due to a strike called by opposition parties to protest at last Friday's killing of Murtaza Bhutto, brother of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on September 10, was 36.9700/37.1549 to the dollar. The premium on the foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 8.90 percent from the opening at 9.20 percent. -- Ibrahim Khan 9221-5685192
